paper.title: Enclosing zeros of continuous functions
paper.venue: ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software 21(3), 327-344 (TOMS 748, Sep 1995)

code.commit: netlib TOMS archive 748.gz (downloaded 2026-11-26, 7457 bytes compressed, 36800 bytes uncompressed; sha256 not recorded by scout)
code.note: One shell-style file with five members, separated by lines 'C*** filename': driver.f, enclofx.f, exdrive.f, testdata, testout. Scout split them with python into /tmp/scout-wake/toms/748/parts/ (not committed). driver.f reads NPROB and N from stdin (testdata gives the 154 pairs), calls INIT, RROOT and prints 'PROBLEM NUMBER ... COMPUTED ROOT = ...'. testout is the shipped reference run in the same format. Needs a Fortran 77 or 90 compiler; the rerun should provision gfortran in the sandbox (see the micromamba path noted by rerun, commit 0e3ea70). The companion paper also lists a test-run table, which scout has not read.

field: numerics (bracketing root finding and interval enclosure)

claim.location: The shipped reference run testout, first block: 'PROBLEM NUMBER 1 WITH PROBLEM PARAMETER 1' followed by 'COMPUTED ROOT = 1.8954942670340'. The driver runs the problem list in testdata in order; the first pair is '1 1'.

reference.file: 748/parts/testout (member of the 748.gz shell-style archive, between the 'C*** testout' marker and the end of the file)

claim.metric: ROOT printed by driver.f for NPROB=1, N=1 (first line of testdata), compared with 1.8954942670340.
claim.paper_value: Shipped testout: 1.8954942670340. The companion paper's table has not been read, so no paper value is used.

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. The algorithm stops when the bracket width is at most 2*TOLE, with NEPS=1000 and machine precision, so a converged double-precision run should agree with the shipped value to roughly machine precision (about 1e-13 here). 1e-8 absolute allows for compiler and libm differences and is far below any plausible error in a different root. Not to be loosened after any run.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 1 second for the first problem; the whole testdata list (154 pairs) takes a few seconds.
cost.data_size: None; the test problems are defined in INIT and FUNC in the shipped source.
cost.data_licence: No data. Netlib TOMS code under the archive's ACM licence; the rerun should record the licence text it finds in the archive.

why: A 1995 Fortran root-finder with interval enclosure ships its test driver, test data and reference output; the claimed root is a computed bracketing-method output for a test problem whose root is not stated in closed form in the archive (the problem definition has not been checked by scout; the rerun should confirm).
